scope: Independent review of all 18 provided PNGs and motion.json timestamps/events. No game source or key read. This is a sampled simulation sequence review, not a real-time playback, touch-input, or actual-device FPS test.
overall_reason: Hit flash, visible HUD controls and sampled wake/camera continuity are adequate. I would not accept the impact-effects polish gate yet: the event identified as a large explosion reads mainly as a thin ring and tiny bright dot, with weak scale distinction from the small impact. Smoke is visibly transient but remains a chain of separate small puffs.

evidence: At 0.1 and 0.2 seconds in both profiles the player becomes an unmistakable bright-white silhouette; hull text/bar falls from 35% to 27% and instruction changes to RETURN TO BASE. By 0.4 seconds the plane returns to its normal blue-gray material, consistent with hitFlash returning to zero in metadata.
The small impact at 0.1 seconds is a narrow yellow ring with tiny center. It expands/fades by 0.2 and is no longer prominent at 0.4 seconds.

The event marked actual large explosion at 1.0 seconds is again a thin yellow ring and small pale center, somewhat larger than the earlier ring but without a strong fire mass or visually dominant impact core. By 1.5 seconds it leaves scattered small faint particles. At phone display scale the major-impact significance is weak.
hit_flash_and_impact_recognition.recommendation: Retain the clear brief player-white flash. Give the large explosion a visibly larger bright core, short shaped fire/debris phase and wider softer smoke development so event scale is recognizable without metadata.

smoke_fading.qualification: Pass for evident lifecycle, not high effects polish.
evidence: The small impact haze/ring becomes less visible across 0.1–0.6 seconds. The old trail is faint while newer puffs stay brighter near the damaged aircraft.

Around the large event, particles change from 47 at 1.0/1.5 seconds to 17 at 2.0 seconds; no fire/ring remain at 2.0 seconds according to metadata. Images correspondingly show only faint scattered haze and the ongoing damaged-aircraft trail.

The trail persists through 3.0 seconds behind the 27%-hull aircraft; this is consistent with continued emission rather than proof old smoke fails to expire. Individual puffs remain regularly spaced dots instead of a continuous expanding plume.
smoke_fading.recommendation: Vary puff size/spacing and expand while lowering opacity. Review denser samples around 1.0–2.0 seconds if precise decay smoothness must be certified.

evidence: Carrier wake stays connected behind its far end as the ship shifts upward/right through early samples and leaves the top of the view.
Smaller ships retain their pale trailing wakes as they cross the screen; the lower/right ship at 2.0 seconds has a connected wake aligned behind its direction of travel.
No sampled disconnected wake fragments or reversed wake direction are evident in either profile. Wake shape remains paired blurred streaks, with limited turbulence or widening.
wake_continuity.recommendation: Preserve attachment; improve widening/dissipation and breakup for material realism. Sparse samples cannot rule out between-frame popping.

camera_motion.qualification: Pass for sampled trajectory/coherence; smooth interpolation cannot be established from these sparse stills.
evidence: Player starts well left/below screen center, moves toward center over 0.1–0.6 seconds, and remains near center while heading turns from -0.4 toward 2.876 radians through 1.5 seconds.
Carrier and other world objects shift coherently while HUD anchors remain fixed. At 2.0 and 3.0 seconds player stays near the same central screen location as world scenery moves rightward.

Initial recentering is substantial: metadata camera moves approximately 54 units left and 37 down in the first 0.1 seconds. This may feel brisk, but the supplied samples alone do not justify a jitter or comfort claim.
camera_motion.recommendation: If camera comfort matters, inspect continuous playback around initial recentering and the turn. No actual phone performance inference made.

evidence: Bomb 2/2 and Fire remain high-contrast and consistently placed on the right in all 18 captures. Hull and heat bars stay visible at upper left; objective text stays on dark backing.

A ship moves behind the translucent Bomb control near 3.0 seconds, but the label remains legible. Right-edge aircraft is partly obscured near 1.5 seconds, which affects world visibility more than button visibility.
The small 27% hull number and heat bar are readable at provided size; steering controls or touch feedback are not represented, so their usability cannot be judged.
control_visibility.recommendation: Keep stable dark backing and test with actual touch interaction separately; sampled visual visibility passes.

profile_comparison: Both profiles preserve the same timing/state progression and essential flash/HUD/wake cues. Fallback is softer and omits much surface foam, reducing texture richness while keeping action readable. No timing values were interpreted as actual phone FPS.
priorities: Improve large-versus-small impact differentiation before claiming polished motion effects.
Break up the dotted smoke trail into expanding overlapping puffs without hiding the aircraft.
Keep wake continuity and clear flash lifecycle; inspect continuous playback only for unresolved interpolation/comfort questions.
